subject.title: TUI: Support Shift+Enter for newline (Enter to send)

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this by documenting the current pi-tui multiline bindings, or should it add a public TUI keybinding preference for send versus newline behavior?
rationale: Current main already gets newline insertion from pi-tui, but a configurable send/newline bridge would create a new public config/CLI surface that repository policy says needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Document Current Bindings
options.body: Update TUI docs and /help for Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and fallback composition, while deferring configurable send keys to a separately sponsored design.

options.title: Add Configurable TUI Keybindings
options.body: Expose a documented config/CLI bridge into pi-tui keybindings with focused tests and upgrade guidance, accepting the new compatibility surface.

options.title: Keep Current Behavior Undocumented
options.body: Close or leave this unchanged only if maintainers intentionally reject additional TUI keybinding docs and configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Document Current Bindings
recommendation.body: Update TUI docs and /help for Shift+Enter, Ctrl+J, terminal limitations, and fallback composition, while deferring configurable send keys to a separately sponsored design.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-history owner for the TUI wrapper/docs surface and already provided the prior maintainer-facing scope note on this issue.
